main.title: Chicory: A Colorful Tale
main.subtitle: A magical brush changes the world
main.summary: Chicory: A Colorful Tale is an adventure video game by indie developer Greg Lobanov and published by Finji.

cards.heading: A magical brush and a world without colour
cards.text: Chicory: A Colorful Tale is an adventure video game by indie developer Greg Lobanov and published by Finji. It was released for Microsoft Windows, macOS, PlayStation 4, and PlayStation 5 in June 2021, for Nintendo Switch in December 2021, and for Xbox One and Xbox Series X and Series S in May 2023. The game features an anthropomorphic dog with a magical paintbrush, which is used to color the game world. Chicory: A Colorful Tale received "universal acclaim" from critics.

cards.heading: Painting while exploring
cards.text: Players paint directly onto surfaces as they explore. The brush activates objects, opens paths and leaves visible marks around the world. There is no score judging the quality of a drawing, so players can choose their own colours and patterns.

cards.heading: Puzzles that respond to colour
cards.text: Puzzles use the way paint interacts with plants, water, light and other objects. A brushstroke can make something grow or reveal a route. Solving these problems also leaves the player?s own colour choices visible in the environment.

cards.heading: Chicory and creative expectations
cards.text: The previous brush wielder, Chicory, faces anxiety, comparison and the expectations attached to her work. The player?s freedom to paint sits alongside a story about the pressure of being seen as an artist. Their relationship explores both the pleasure of making things and the fear of not being good enough.

main.title: Game Builder Garage
main.subtitle: Build a game by connecting its parts
main.summary: Game Builder Garage is Nintendo's visual programming game, released for Nintendo Switch on 11 June 2021.

cards.heading: Build a game by connecting its parts
cards.text: Game Builder Garage is Nintendo's visual programming game, released for Nintendo Switch on 11 June 2021. It introduces game-making through Nodon, characters that represent inputs, objects, logic and other functions. Connecting them creates working relationships: an analogue stick can move a person, a button can trigger an action and a condition can change what happens next. Guided lessons build complete small games before a free programming mode lets the player assemble an idea from the same components.

cards.heading: A wire turns an input into an action
cards.text: The connections make the cause of an action visible. A Stick Nodon reports movement from the controller, while an Object Nodon represents something in the game world. Linking the appropriate ports passes information between them. Testing the result shows whether that relationship behaves as intended. When it does not, the player can return to the programming view and adjust the connection or a value. The process turns an apparently simple action on screen into a set of parts that can be inspected and altered.

cards.heading: Test the idea and change the connection
cards.text: Seven interactive lessons introduce different kinds of games, while additional puzzles explain particular Nodon and their uses. The system can work with motion controls and other Switch inputs, and supports projects for several players. Creations can be shared through codes so that someone else can try them. The garage places learning inside the cycle of making and testing: a lesson supplies a useful pattern, and the next experiment asks what happens when the player changes the objects or relationships within it.

main.title: Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart
main.subtitle: Rift Apart Turns Fast Loading into a Directing Gag
main.summary: The spectacle needs to remain readable.

cards.heading: Choosing which things stand out
cards.text: Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart follows Ratchet and Rivet through worlds connected by dimensional rifts. Its fast traversal and varied weapons share the screen with dense visual detail. Insomniac researcher Michele Zorrilla described contrast options that help distinguish characters, hazards, collectibles and interactive objects. Background desaturation can keep important objects prominent while preserving the setting.

cards.heading: Changing time and button demands
cards.text: The same design work changes demands on movement and timing. Zorrilla describes shortcuts for slowing the game to selected speeds, then returning it to normal. Other options replace repeated presses or sustained holds with different firing behaviours. The Enforcer's two trigger stages, for example, can retain their separate functions while the method of repeating fire changes. Accessibility here reaches into the actions themselves. A player can have more time to interpret a traversal sequence or fewer simultaneous physical demands without the studio having to remove the sequence from the adventure.

cards.heading: Another Lombax, another setting
cards.text: Creative director Marcus Smith introduced Rivet as a Lombax resistance fighter from another dimension, placing her against Emperor Nefarious. His reveal pairs new locations with alternate versions of familiar places such as Sargasso and Torren IV. It also announces Mark Mothersbaugh as composer. The dimensional premise therefore gives the series several ways to change its presentation: another protagonist, altered environments and a new musical contribution. The familiar Ratchet and Clank pairing becomes part of a larger set of perspectives rather than the only way into the story.

cards.heading: Ratchet, Rivet and their arsenal
cards.text: The game shares many gameplay similarities with Ratchet & Clank (2016) and other entries in the series. It retains elements of previous Ratchet & Clank games, such as strafing, gunplay, collection of bolts, automatic weapon and health upgrades, manual Raritanium weapon upgrading and gadgets. The main playable character is Ratchet. He is accompanied by his robotic friend and sidekick Clank, who is hung on his back. Additionally, the game has a playable female Lombax named Rivet, as well as a robot similar to Clank, Kit. The player navigates Ratchet and Rivet through diverse environments across a multitude of levels, defeating enemies with an array of varied weapons and gadgets, and traversing obstacles to complete key mission objectives.

cards.heading: Crossing dimensional rifts
cards.text: The game introduces to the series the concept of real-time near instantaneous travel between different areas, planets and other worlds within gameplay scenes via a system of inter-dimensional portals. In order for the player to utilize this feature, a new mechanic dubbed the "Rift Tether" is introduced in Ratchet and Rivet's arsenal that pulls them from one side of a portal to another, allowing them to move quickly between points. The game features the return of planets explored in previous entries with a dimensional twist, through their alternate counterparts, alongside new planets not seen previously in the franchise.  The game features enhanced mobility and traversal options with the addition of moves such as dashing and wall running. In addition, the game's arsenal features a mix of brand new weapons and returning classics from prior installments.

cards.heading: Linking traversal moves
cards.text: On building the game's traversal mechanics, there was a learning opportunity for Insomniac Games to leverage their experiences from past titles they have developed, to improve upon and expand on the traversal mechanics in Rift Apart. Smith stated that "I think the lessons that we learned from Sunset Overdrive and Spider-Man whereas we might've just had a hook shot somewhere, now we're having areas where you can Hook Shot and then use Phantom Dash and then wall run and then rift tether and it flows together really nicely".

cards.heading: A retro-futuristic score
cards.text: Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart features an original score composed primarily by Mark Mothersbaugh and Wataru Hokoyama. Known for his works in Hotel Transylvania, The Lego Movie, Thor: Ragnarok and The Croods: A New Age, Mothersbaugh was contacted early in the game's development. Insomniac Games wanted the soundtrack to evoke a retro-futuristic sound; this approach informed the sound direction, and led to their subsequent search for the right composer to fulfill this vision. They requested Mothersbaugh who later agreed to compose for the game. Mothersbaugh went for a more experimental sound using various instruments including synthesizers to compose the score. By combining eclectic synth sounds with orchestral beats, Mothersbaugh was able to deliver a more cinematic sound experience in line with the guiding vision of the studio.

main.title: Mario Golf: Super Rush
main.subtitle: A golf shot followed by a race
main.summary: Mario Golf: Super Rush is Camelot's Switch golf game, released on 25 June 2021.

cards.heading: A golf shot followed by a race
cards.text: Mario Golf: Super Rush is Camelot's Switch golf game, released on 25 June 2021. Familiar Mario characters play traditional rounds alongside modes that turn the trip between shots into part of the competition. In Speed Golf, players hit the ball and then run after it, trying to complete a course quickly while navigating obstacles and rivals. The careful preparation of a stroke meets a much less orderly journey across the fairway, making the space between the tee and the next lie part of the action.

cards.heading: Read the course before the swing
cards.text: Standard golf remains centered on finishing each hole in as few strokes as possible. A shot gauge and scanning tools help assess direction, slope and elevation before choosing a club and swing. Button controls are joined by an option to imitate the swing through motion controls. Special Shots add character-specific effects that can disturb another player's plan. The player can choose how much of that extra interference belongs in a match, keeping the underlying course-reading task visible beneath the more theatrical abilities.

cards.heading: The next hole becomes a shared scramble
cards.text: Speed Golf combines the time taken to run with the consequences of each shot, so a long strike also determines the route the character must travel next. Battle Golf condenses the contest into an arena where players race to finish three holes. A separate adventure follows a Mii through golf challenges and development. Motoi Sakuraba's score accompanies the different formats. Super Rush uses the same ball-and-course foundation for both a measured sporting round and a race in which reaching the next shot becomes a challenge of its own.

main.title: Scarlet Nexus
main.summary: Scarlet Nexus is a 2021 action role-playing game developed by Bandai Namco Studios and Tose, and published by Bandai Namco Entertainment.

cards.heading: A society shaped by psychic powers
cards.text:
Scarlet Nexus is a 2021 action role-playing game developed by Bandai Namco Studios and Tose, and published by Bandai Namco Entertainment.

The game is set in the near future in an alternate reality where humanity has developed technology and formed a society based on substances found in human brains that grant extrasensory superpowers.

cards.heading: Psychokinesis and borrowed abilities
cards.text: Scarlet Nexus is an action role-playing game played from a third-person perspective. Players can assume control of either Yuito Sumeragi or Kasane Randall, members of the Other Suppression Force (OSF) who are tasked to defend New Himuka from creatures known as the Others. While they are equipped with short-range weapons like a sword, both Yuito and Kasane possess the ability of psychokinesis, allowing them to hurl objects and debris at hostile enemies. The protagonist's powers can be upgraded through accessing the "brain map", which serves as the game's skill tree. As players progress through the story, they encounter different party members who assist them in combat. Each companion has their own unique combat abilities, which can then be temporarily borrowed by the protagonists through an ability named "brain link", powered by the Struggle Arms System (SAS).

cards.heading: Designing a brain-punk world
cards.text: Scarlet Nexus was co-developed by Bandai Namco Studios and Tose. Keita Iizuka is the game's producer while Kenji Anabuki served as the game's director, both of whom have worked on the Tales series. According to Iizuka, the term "Scarlet Nexus" means "red connection" or "red bond". Therefore, "objects or persons connected with red lines represent a big part in the visuals and key art" of the game. Artist Masakazu Yamashiro combined organic lifeforms and mechanical elements together in order to create unique design for the Others, the protagonists' enemies. In the game, while the Others invade merely to consume human brains, humanity has already developed a system to forecast their invasion. Game director Kenji Anabuki compared them to natural disasters that humans need to co-exist with. Given the game's theme, story and setting, Bandai Namco called Scarlet Nexus a "brain punk" game.

main.title: Humankind
main.subtitle: Humankind Treats Civilization as a Sequence of Identities
main.summary: On August 17, 2021 Amplitude Studios released Humankind on PC.

cards.heading: Humankind Treats Civilization as a Sequence of Identities
cards.text: Amplitude Studios released Humankind on PC on August 17, 2021. The historical 4X strategy game lets players adopt a new culture in each era, accumulating traits and priorities through the campaign. Fame earned from achievements determines the winner when the game ends. Building a successful civilisation can therefore involve changing its specialisation over time.

cards.heading: Choosing a culture in each era
cards.text: Humankind is a 4X game comparable to the Civilization series. Players lead their civilization across six major eras of human civilization, following an initial nomadic Neolithic phase, directing how the civilization should expand, developing cities, controlling military and other types of units as they interact with other civilizations on the virtual planet, randomly generated at the start of a new game. A distinguishing feature of Humankind is that within each of the eras, the player selects one of ten civilization types based on historical societies; this selection offers both bonuses and penalties to how the player can build out the civilization. Because a player can select different civilizations as templates to build upon, there exist potentially one million different civilization patterns that a player can ultimately develop.

cards.heading: Fame determines the winner
cards.text: During the game, the players gain resources for their civilization, similar to Endless Legend, which includes food, industry, gold, science, and influence; these support different aspects of the civilization, rather than acting as interchangeable trade goods. Money can be used to buy construction projects outright, while influence is tracked separately. Humankind also includes Fame, which is earned by feats within the game, for example, accumulating influence or gold, destroying units, being the first civilization to discover certain technologies, or build world wonders. Fame is a persistent measure of a civilization's relative success compared to other civilizations, and can impact later decisions in the game. Unlike games like Civilization where there can be multiple victory conditions, victory in Humankind is based solely on the Fame score after a pre-determined number of turns, or other events that trigger end-game.

cards.heading: Cities, territories and tactical battles
cards.text: Building out cities follows a similar model from Amplitude's Endless Legend game, a continent in Humankind will have multiple territories on it, and the player will only be able to build one city in that territory. Over time, they can expand that city, adding farms and other outlying resources as well as more dense urban areas closer to the city center. This allows the creation of large metropolises within each territory. Players may also need to engage in combat with enemy forces. When this occurs, the game uses a tactical role-playing game approach for detailed resolution of these battles, giving the player a chance to take advantage of terrain and special abilities of their units. Within these skirmishes, combat proceeds in rounds within the strategic turn, and larger battles can continue across multiple strategic turns, with reinforcements joining the fighting.

main.title: Psychonauts 2
main.summary: Psychonauts 2 is a 2021 platform game developed by Double Fine and published by Xbox Game Studios.

cards.heading: Raz returns in a new Psychonauts adventure
cards.text: Psychonauts 2 is a 2021 platform game developed by Double Fine and published by Xbox Game Studios. The game was announced at The Game Awards 2015 ceremony, and released on August 25, 2021 for PlayStation 4, Windows, Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S, and on May 24, 2022 for Linux and macOS.

cards.heading: A mystery inside other minds
cards.text: Like the game's predecessor, the player controls Raz, a young acrobat who is training to become a Psychonaut, a member of an international task force that uses their psychic abilities to stop those that perform nefarious deeds with their own psychic forces. Within Psychonauts 2, which directly follows the events of the interstitial virtual reality game, Psychonauts in the Rhombus of Ruin (2017), the Psychonauts try to learn who was really behind the capture of their leader, unveiling a deep mystery surrounding the organization's founding and Raz's family history. To uncover the mystery, Raz enters the mindscapes of various characters to discover clues. Within these mindscapes, Raz can perform a variety of new and returning psychic abilities that allow him to maneuver through their often-twisted minds and battle the mental creatures they produce.

main.title: Australia's games become playable again
main.subtitle: 2021: ACMI describes Play It Again II

cards.heading: A box is a beginning
cards.text: A box in a museum can name a game without letting anyone play it. Writing for ACMI in 2021, digital preservation technician Mar Cruz described a project to recover the playable history of Australasian games from the 1990s. Shadowrun, Powerslide and Flight of the Amazon Queen demonstrated the variety involved. Their different machines and software requirements complicated access. Play It Again II joined the museum to university researchers and the Australian research network AARNet, bringing the work of conservation into contact with computing infrastructure.

cards.heading: Keep the tested environment
cards.text: Cruz described a way to make that variety manageable: gather emulated environments through EaaSI, then test which suited each game. Finding and installing an emulator was only the beginning; the team needed to compare how it represented the experience. A reusable environment could carry those decisions forward instead of requiring each visitor or researcher to begin again. The museum's task extended from collecting a game to preparing the circumstances in which someone could encounter it, with testing becoming part of the collection's care.

cards.heading: The reader needs preserving too
cards.text: In 2023, Cynde Moya, Helen Stuckey, Melanie Swalwell and Denise de Vries reported on fifty selected games. First came copies of the data on floppies, discs and cartridges, each demanding suitable tools. Some imaging devices came from hobbyist projects whose continued production depended on people and obtainable components. The preservation chain therefore included the tools used to read the original object. Saving software involved maintaining that practical knowledge as well as finding a place for the resulting data in a collection.

cards.heading: Configure for this particular game
cards.text: The same report returned to a familiar problem for anyone who had configured a 1990s PC: the game expected particular graphics and sound hardware. The Dame Was Loaded posed difficulties with its live-action video. The researchers compared emulators and working vintage machines while adjusting performance. They also used separate community emulators for systems EaaSI did not yet include. A working configuration was something to discover and document. Making a museum game playable required attention to its individual demands, beyond simply keeping its files.

main.title: Tales of Arise
main.summary: Tales of Arise is a 2021 action role-playing game developed and published by Bandai Namco Entertainment.

cards.heading: Alphen and Shionne cross a divided world
cards.text: Tales of Arise is a 2021 action role-playing game developed and published by Bandai Namco Entertainment. The seventeenth main entry in the Tales series, the game follows a man and a woman from the opposing worlds of Dahna and Rena and their journey to end the Renans' oppression of the Dahnan people.

cards.heading: Evade, counter and strike together
cards.text: Like previous games in the series, Tales of Arise is an action role-playing game, although its gameplay has gone through alterations as part of its development goals while retaining the basic Tales battle system, dubbed the Linear Motion Battle System. The game has a large focus on evading and countering, with Tales of Graces, a 2009 entry praised for its combat, cited as inspiration. Unlike many previous titles in the series, the game does not feature local co-op control sharing of characters, with the development team deciding to focus on various interactions between characters in combat. This includes the addition of the "Boost Strike" feature, allowing multiple party members to perform destructive attacks together under certain conditions.

cards.heading: Five realms under Renan rule
cards.text: Arise takes place in a setting divided between the medieval world of Dahna and the advanced world of Rena. Three centuries ago, the Renans based on Rena's artificial moon Lenegis invaded and conquered Dahna, enslaving the population and dividing the land into five isolated realms: the barren and fiery Calaglia, the dark and cold Cyslodia, the Elde Menancia plains, the Mahag Saar mountains, and the Ganath Haros rainforests. Periodically, the "Crown Contest" is held to decide which among the five Lords is chosen to become the next Renan Sovereign.

cards.heading: Rebuilding the Tales formula
cards.text: According to producer Yusuke Tomizawa, development of Arise began before the announcement of the Definitive Edition of Tales of Vesperia in 2018. Beginning development under the codename "Arise", the aim was to reevaluate and evolve the Tales franchise formula. The game's title derived from its codename as it best exemplified both the game's story themes and the team's wishes. While previous Tales games used a dedicated in-house engine, Arise was built using Unreal Engine 4, allowing much higher graphical quality compared to earlier entries. Character models and movement were also improved, with the team aiming at the same level of quality found in 3D films and television. While the previous game Tales of Berseria had been a cross-generation game for PlayStation 3 and PlayStation 4, Arise was made exclusively for modern hardware. Tomizawa stated that, while the team was aiming for a level of quality that can be enjoyed globally, the game would not neglect its Japanese fans.

main.title: WarioWare: Get It Together!
main.subtitle: The characters enter the microgames
main.summary: WarioWare: Get It Together! is Intelligent Systems' Switch party game, released on 10 September 2021.

cards.heading: The characters enter the microgames
cards.text: WarioWare: Get It Together! is Intelligent Systems' Switch party game, released on 10 September 2021. Wario and his friends are pulled inside their latest game device and must take part in its rapid microgames themselves. A short instruction appears, a few seconds are available and the chosen character has to make the necessary change on screen. The familiar WarioWare rhythm remains, but the cast now stands between the player's input and the task, turning character abilities into a new source of variation.

cards.heading: One instruction, several ways to solve it
cards.text: A direction stick and one button control the action, but each character uses them differently. Wario flies and shoulder-charges, while 18-Volt throws discs from a fixed position and moves by catching rings. The same microgame can therefore require a different solution when another character appears. A target might be reached through direct contact or a projectile, depending on the current member of the crew. Success demands reading the brief instruction and immediately translating it into the tools that particular character can provide.

cards.heading: A crew chosen for the next few seconds
cards.text: The story can be played cooperatively by two people, with further party activities supporting up to four. A growing cast and challenge modes give completed microgames new combinations of abilities and constraints. Ko Takeuchi and Waki Shigeta's character art preserves the series' expressive, comic identity. The central change is small but far-reaching: each miniature task now has both a rule and a performer. Learning the cast becomes another way to improve at the games, and a familiar instruction can feel new when it arrives with an inconvenient character.
